ai.literal: Virtue, wealth, pleasure, and fear for life—of these four, having examined the nature, (a person) is to be trusted.
ai.translation: A person should be chosen and trusted only after testing them through the fourfold trials of virtue, wealth, pleasure, and the fear of losing one's life.
ai.modern: அறம், பொருள், இன்பம், உயிர் மேல் உள்ள பயம் ஆகிய நான்கு வழிகளிலும் ஒருவருடைய குணத்தை ஆராய்ந்து அறிந்த பிறகே அவரைத் தேர்ந்தெடுக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the four essential tests to evaluate a person's character before employing them in a position of trust. The tests examine how the person responds to the pull of virtue (அறம்), the temptation of wealth (பொருள்), the desire for pleasure (இன்பம்), and the instinct of self-preservation or fear of death (உயிரச்சம்). By observing their behavior under these four pressures, their true nature (திறம்) is revealed. Only those who remain steadfast and upright through all four trials should be trusted (தேறப்படும்) with responsibility.

ai.literal: Born in a noble family, having freed oneself from faults, fearing blame, he who possesses a sense of shame—specifically pointing to him is trust.
ai.translation: Trust should be placed only in one who is born of a noble family, remains free from faults, fears disgrace, and possesses a strong sense of shame.
ai.modern: நல்ல குடியில் பிறந்து, குற்றங்களிலிருந்து விலகி, பழிச்சொல்லுக்கு அஞ்சி, நாணமுடையவனாக இருக்கும் ஒருவனையே ஆராய்ந்து தேர்வு செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the essential qualities of a person who can be trusted and selected for a position of responsibility. First, they must come from a noble lineage (kuṭi), which instills a natural inclination toward virtue. Second, they must have freed themselves from faults (kuṟṟam). Third, they must fear blame or disgrace (vaṭu). Finally, they must possess a strong sense of shame (nāṇ) regarding wrong actions. Selecting such a person ensures reliability and integrity.

ai.literal: Rare things having learned, fault those who are free from, even in, when examining, absence is rare indeed of ignorance.
ai.translation: Even among those who have learned rare works and are free from faults, when examined closely, the complete absence of ignorance is rare indeed.
ai.modern: அரிய நூல்களைக் கற்று, குற்றங்கள் இல்லாதவராக விளங்குபவர்களிடத்திலும் கூட, ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்கும் போது, அறியாமை இல்லாமல் இருப்பது என்பது மிகவும் அரிதானதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the realistic limits of human perfection, which is a vital lesson when choosing people for key duties. The poet explains that even when we look at highly learned individuals who seem entirely free of faults, a deep and close examination will still reveal some trace of ignorance. The word 'veḷiṟu' literally means whiteness or blankness, beautifully representing a blank spot of ignorance or folly in an otherwise brilliant mind. Therefore, expecting a complete absence of flaws in anyone is unrealistic, and one must learn to evaluate others by balancing their great merits against their minor shortcomings.

ai.literal: Good qualities having examined, faults also having examined, among them the excess having examined, that which is greater, to accept.
ai.translation: Weigh a person's merits and weigh their faults; then, assessing which of the two is greater, form your judgment of them.
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய நற்குணங்களை ஆராய்ந்து, அவருடைய குற்றங்களையும் ஆராய்ந்து, அவற்றுள் எது அதிகமாக இருக்கிறதோ அதை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டு அவரைப் பற்றி முடிவு செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet provides a highly practical and realistic method for evaluating people before placing trust or responsibility in them. The author advises us to first examine a person's virtues (குணம்) and then objectively examine their faults (குற்றம்). Since no human is entirely perfect, we must compare the two and see which side outweighs the other (மிகை). Our final decision to accept or trust them (கொளல்) should be based on whichever side is predominant (மிக்க).

ai.literal: For greatness and the other, lowliness, their respective action indeed is the touchstone.
ai.translation: A person's own deeds are the touchstone that measures both their greatness and their lowliness.
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய பெருமைக்கும் மற்றதான சிறுமைக்கும் அவரவர் செய்யும் செயல்களே உரைகல்லாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how to evaluate a person's true character and worth. The poet uses the metaphor of a touchstone, which is a stone used to test the purity of gold. A person's own actions serve as this touchstone, revealing whether they possess true greatness or lowliness. Rather than relying on birth, words, or appearance, one must look at a person's deeds to judge their true value.

ai.literal: Trusting those who have no relations, avoid; for they, attachment do not have, will not feel ashamed of disgrace.
ai.translation: Avoid choosing or trusting those who have no family ties; since they have no attachments, they will not fear disgrace.
ai.modern: உறவினர்கள் இல்லாதவர்களைத் தேர்ந்தெடுத்து நம்புவதைத் தவிர்க்க வேண்டும்; ஏனெனில், அவர்களுக்குப் பற்று இல்லாததால் அவர்கள் பழிக்கு அஞ்சமாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns a leader against employing or trusting individuals who have no family ties or social attachments. The key words are 'பற்று இலர்' (those without attachments) and 'நாணார் பழி' (those who do not fear disgrace). A person with family and social connections is naturally restrained by the fear of bringing shame upon their loved ones. In contrast, someone completely detached from such relationships lacks this moral anchor and is more likely to commit dishonorable acts without any fear of public blame. Therefore, choosing such people for responsible positions must be avoided.

ai.literal: Taking affection as support, trusting those who do not know knowledge, will bring all foolishness.
ai.translation: Trusting and choosing those who lack wisdom, merely out of personal affection, will bring every kind of folly.
ai.modern: அன்பையே அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டு, அறிவு இல்லாதவர்களைத் தேர்ந்தெடுத்து நம்புவது, எல்லாவிதமான அறியாமையையும் துன்பத்தையும் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against choosing or trusting people for important duties based solely on personal attachment. The word 'காதன்மை' refers to affection, and 'கந்தா' means taking it as a support or pillar. If a leader trusts those who lack wisdom ('அறிவறியார்') simply because they love them, it will result in complete ruin, bringing every form of foolishness ('பேதைமை எல்லாம்') to their endeavors.

ai.literal: He who does not examine, another person, he who trusted, to his lineage, unending, distress, will give.
ai.translation: Trusting a stranger without examining their character will bring endless distress to one's entire lineage.
ai.modern: ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்காமல் ஒருவரை நம்பித் தெளிந்தவனுடைய செயலே அவனது பரம்பரைக்கும் நீங்காத துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the severe consequences of blind trust. The word 'தேரான்' describes someone who fails to investigate or analyze a person's character before employing or relying on them. If one blindly trusts ('தெளிந்தான்') such an unexamined stranger ('பிறனை'), the resulting failure does not stop with them. It brings endless, incurable misery ('தீரா இடும்பை') that plagues their entire lineage and descendants ('வழிமுறை').

ai.literal: Do not trust anyone without examining; after examining, trust the trustworthy thing.
ai.translation: Do not place trust in anyone without first testing them; once you have tested them, trust that which is found to be trustworthy.
ai.modern: யாரையும் ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்காமல் தெளிந்து நம்பக் கூடாது; அவ்வாறு ஆராய்ந்த பிறகு, நம்பத்தகுந்தவரை நம்ப வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the crucial sequence of testing before trusting. The poet uses two distinct but related verbs: 'தேர்' (to examine or test) and 'தேறு' (to trust or become clear). We are warned never to trust anyone blindly without a thorough prior examination. Once that careful testing is complete, we must confidently rely on the person or course of action that has proven to be genuinely trustworthy.

ai.literal: Trusting one who has not examined, and suspecting towards one who has been trusted, will give unending sorrow.
ai.translation: Trusting someone without prior examination, and harboring suspicion toward someone who has already been trusted and chosen, will both yield unending misery.
ai.modern: ஆராயாமல் ஒருவரை நம்புவதும், அவ்வாறு ஆராய்ந்து தெளிந்து தேர்ந்தெடுத்தவரிடம் சந்தேகம் கொள்வதும் நீங்காத துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights two fatal errors in judgment and relationship management. First, trusting or employing someone without thoroughly examining their character and capabilities leads to disaster. Second, once a person has been carefully examined, trusted, and selected, constantly doubting or suspecting them destroys the relationship and ruins the work. Both of these actions are equally harmful and will result in endless, incurable misery.
